keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area (infobox: none) and no boundary; it names the seat in Surakarta and, as territory, Karanganyar and Wonogiri, so the outline is three discs (about 12 + 25 + 20 km radius). The page says the realm was 'relatively 49% of the Nagara Agung' after 1830, a figure that is unclear. The larger Mangkunegaran lands of later years (Colomadu, Karanganyar, Wonogiri, Baturetno) are not on the page.

ledger.note: 17 March 1757: the Mangkunegaran begins. Infobox 'Treaty of Salatiga: 1757'; the text: 'signed on 17 March 1757 in Salatiga'; 'It was established in 1757 by Raden Mas Said, when he submitted his army to Pakubuwono III in February'; he 'was given an appanage of 4000 households' and signed a treaty with the VOC the same year. Karanganyar and Wonogiri are the territory the page names.

ledger.note: 19 August 1945: the Mangkunegaran joins the Republic. The rulers 'pledged to have their realms be part of the Unitary Republic of Indonesia on 19 August 1945' (royal decree 1 September 1945); the line continues as a devolved monarchy within Indonesia.

certainty.note: The page names no boundary; the appanage was counted in households and the territories were intermixed with Surakarta's.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch at the request of the surakarta-sunanate dossier (loss of 17 March 1757, counterpart 'mangkunegaran'). One page opened. Unsettled: (1) the page gives no area or boundary, so the outline is three discs; (2) the page says the VOC treaty of 1757 gave Mangkunegara the right to keep his own army ('Mangkunegaran Legion', no dates) and records no vassal tie to Surakarta or the Company, so no vassal event is recorded here (the suzerain dossiers - dutch-east-india-company, dutch-east-indies - are for that); (3) the end: the infobox says 'Integration with Indonesia: present', the text a pledge of 19 August 1945 and the Special Region of Surakarta, whose abolition in 1946 is not on the page; the dossier ends at the pledge; (4) the page gives no British or Japanese events for the Mangkunegaran; (5) the capital's coordinates are approximate; (6) no rulers strip: the page lists ten rulers (Mangkunegara I 17 March 1757 - 28 December 1795 first), only the first was read.
